artists.biography: Thank You Scientist is an eclectic seven piece progressive rock band from New Jersey. Founded by guitarist and band leader Tom Monda, the band self-released an EP in 2011, The Perils of Time Travel, before signing with Coheed and Cambria frontman Claudio Sanchez’s newly launched Evil Ink Records. Their 2012 full length debut, Maps of Non-Existent Places (re-released in 2014), was a critical success, making inroads on the Billboard Hard Rock and Heat-seekers charts, and was eventually named “Album of the Week” by Revolver Magazine in 2014. They followed up in 2016 with the ambitious Stranger Heads Prevail, which cracked the Billboard Top 200. In addition to original guitarist/band leader Tom Monda and vocalist Salvatore Marrano, the band’s lineup has gradually changed to include violinist Ben Karas, bassist Cody McCorry, drummer Faye Fadem, trumpeter Joe Gullace, and saxophonist Sam Greenfield. Thank You Scientist has spent the past several years touring internationally, both as headliners and as direct support for acts such as Coheed and Cambria, Periphery, Haken, Protest the Hero, Devin Townsend, Yes, The Aristocrats, and many more. The band is eager to follow up their 2016 release with their gargantuan third full length record, due in early 2019. Salvatore Marrano – vocals (2009–present) Tom Monda – electric guitar, fretless guitar, shamisen, sitar, vocals, synth, producer (2009–present) Ben Karas – electric violin (2013–present) Cody McCorry – bass, theremin, saw (2015–present) Faye Fadem – drums (2017–present) Sam Greenfield – saxophone (2017–present) Joe Gullace – trumpet (2017–present) Please visit https://www.facebook.com/ThankYouScientist Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Terraformer is the third studio album by progressive rock band Thank You Scientist, released on June 14, 2019, through Evil Ink Records. The album showcases the band’s signature blend of jazz, rock, and progressive elements, characterized by intricate arrangements, dynamic instrumentation, and genre-defying songwriting. Featuring a septet lineup with prominent use of violin, trumpet, and saxophone alongside traditional rock instruments, Terraformer delivers a vibrant and unpredictable sound that balances technical prowess with memorable song structures. The album’s musical style draws from jazz fusion, alternative rock, and progressive metal, resulting in a richly layered and energetic listening experience.

In the context of Thank You Scientist’s discography, Terraformer stands as a creative high point, marking the final appearances of vocalist Salvatore Marrano and drummer Faye Fadem before their departures. The album received strong critical acclaim, with outlets such as Distorted Sound awarding it a perfect 10/10 and Metal Injection and Sonic Perspectives giving it scores of 9/10 and 9.3/10, respectively. Critics praised its ambitious compositions, tight performances, and the seamless integration of jazz and rock influences. While not a mainstream commercial blockbuster, Terraformer solidified Thank You Scientist’s reputation as innovators within the progressive rock scene and remains a standout release in their catalog.
